paragraphs: SAG, SAGA, and IAG solve optimization problems by reusing gradient information from different parts of a dataset. Their convergence has traditionally been explained through separate mathematical arguments, with the original SAG proof particularly complicated. This paper develops one analysis covering all three methods, making their shared behavior easier to understand.

The main setting is finite-sum optimization with smooth, strongly convex objectives. The proof first bounds how old gradient information can become because only some components are sampled at each step. It then builds a Lyapunov function, a mathematical measure of progress, that explicitly accounts for these delays. Together, these steps connect sampling behavior to convergence.

The resulting argument is short and modular, with high-probability guarantees for SAG and SAGA. The authors also describe extensions to non-convex objectives and Markovian sampling. For IAG, the same technique produces the best known convergence rates reported in the abstract, improving earlier bounds. The contribution is therefore both a simpler common explanation and stronger guarantees for an existing algorithm.
icml-2026-a-short-and-unified-convergenc.tldr: A unified proof explains convergence of SAG, SAGA, and IAG while improving known convergence bounds for IAG.

paragraphs: Finding an object in a 3D scene from a spoken or written instruction becomes difficult when several objects fit the description. Traditional 3D visual grounding generally assumes that the instruction identifies a single target. This paper instead defines a task that explicitly permits ambiguous references, bringing incomplete human instructions into the problem formulation.

The proposed framework resolves ambiguity through several rounds of interaction. The model asks clarifying questions, and a person supplies answers about object attributes, spatial relationships, or other relevant context. These exchanges provide additional evidence for selecting the intended object. Asking for clarification becomes part of the grounding process rather than something excluded by the task assumptions.

The authors introduce AmbiRefer3D to support learning this behavior. It contains 47,085 samples and 141,255 question-answer dialogue annotations spanning 7,316 indoor 3D scenes. They also define evaluation measures covering both grounding accuracy and the efficiency of disambiguation across rounds. These contributions establish a way to study not just which object a system selects, but how effectively interaction helps it resolve uncertainty.
icml-2026-ambirefer3d-3d-visual-groundin.tldr: AmbiRefer3D introduces a dataset and interactive framework for resolving ambiguous 3D object references through clarifying questions.

paragraphs: Scientific models learned from data face two challenges highlighted here: neural operators struggle with high-frequency behavior, while incorporating physical constraints can make optimization difficult. APIC combines neural and symbolic modeling in a reconfigurable architecture, allowing different kinds of domain knowledge to be built into the model.

A central mechanism separates gradients used for parameter identification from those used for residual correction. These two optimization paths can interfere with one another, so reducing their interaction helps mitigate conflicting updates. For nonlinear dissipative systems, the authors instantiate the framework using a Generalized Kuramoto-Sivashinsky-Cahn-Hilliard kernel, providing a shared representation for identifying dynamics with sparse structure.

Experiments report substantial accuracy improvements over architectures including CNNs and Transformers on 3D compressible supersonic shock-wave prediction. The authors also report a favorable accuracy–computation tradeoff against state-of-the-art models and adaptability across meteorological and urban traffic datasets. These findings support the value of organizing physical parameter learning and neural correction carefully within one framework, with demonstrated benefits across the evaluated prediction tasks.
icml-2026-apic-orthogonalized-neuro-symb.tldr: APIC combines physical structure and neural correction while separating their optimization paths to improve scientific prediction accuracy and efficiency.

paragraphs: Prediction uncertainty matters differently depending on which action a decision maker takes. Conformal prediction creates sets of plausible outcomes with explicit guarantees, and earlier work connected these sets to risk-averse policies. However, those policies inherited guarantees averaged over decisions, rather than guarantees explicitly conditioned on each chosen action.

This paper introduces action-conditional conformal prediction to address that distinction. It shows how the resulting prediction sets can stand in for the feasible decision space when optimizing action-conditional value-at-risk, a criterion concerned with a quantile of outcomes for a particular action. This connects uncertainty estimation directly to the risk objective used to choose actions.

The authors also develop a finite-sample algorithm based on minimizing pinball loss, linking the theoretical framework to a concrete procedure. Experiments on two real-world datasets show significantly better action-conditional performance than conformal baselines. The stated advance is a stronger alignment between guarantees and individual decisions: uncertainty is evaluated in relation to the action actually taken, rather than only through an aggregate safety statement.
icml-2026-conformal-risk-averse-decision.tldr: The paper connects conformal prediction to risk-averse decisions with guarantees conditioned on each action.

paragraphs: Diffusion Bridge and Flow Matching both learn transformations between distributions, but differences in assumptions and implementation make their relative strengths difficult to assess. This paper places them within a shared theoretical framework and compares implementations with the same architecture, connecting mathematical analysis to controlled empirical comparisons.

Through stochastic optimal control, the authors prove a lower cost function for Diffusion Bridge within their formulation, associating this with more stable and natural trajectories. An optimal-transport analysis also finds that Flow Matching's interpolation coefficients become increasingly ineffective as training data shrink. These results identify reasons that the approaches can behave differently as the available data change.

For experiments, the authors introduce a latent-Transformer Diffusion Bridge architecture and construct a structurally matched Flow Matching model. They evaluate image restoration, translation, and style transfer while varying training-set size and the discrepancy between distributions. The reported findings agree with the theoretical predictions. The contribution is a framework for interpreting the methods' respective advantages and disadvantages, grounded in both a shared mathematical treatment and matched experimental designs.
icml-2026-diffusion-bridge-or-flow-match.tldr: A shared theoretical framework and matched architectures clarify how Diffusion Bridge and Flow Matching compare as data and transformation difficulty vary.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting becomes harder when the process generating the observations changes over time. Mixture-of-experts models can divide prediction work among specialized components, but fixed expert collections and routing without memory limit their ability to handle abrupt changes. Dynamic TMoE addresses both the composition of the expert pool and how experts are selected.

During learning, the framework detects distribution shifts using Maximum Mean Discrepancy. It adds heterogeneous experts when needed and removes redundant ones, allowing model capacity to evolve. Its router combines recurrent state with a repository of anomalies, so expert selection can incorporate temporal context instead of treating each routing decision in isolation.

The framework is designed to use this learned structure and contextual routing without test-time updates. Across nine benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art forecasting results, with reductions of 10.4% in mean squared error and 7.8% in mean absolute error. These findings support combining adaptation of the architecture during learning with memory in routing, rather than relying solely on a fixed collection of specialists.
icml-2026-dynamic-tmoe-a-drift-aware-dyn.tldr: Dynamic TMoE evolves its expert pool during learning and uses temporal routing memory to improve forecasting under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Training a language model to produce Isabelle proofs depends on more than collecting a large raw proof corpus. Such corpora can be highly imbalanced, and Isabelle's specialized proof structure makes general-purpose data selection less effective. This paper focuses on choosing useful training examples and making verifier responses useful during generation.

The selection method evaluates proof data along three dimensions: proof complexity, semantic coverage, and reasoning diversity, collectively called PSR. These criteria produce a compact training subset containing 4,000 examples. At inference time, a separate prompt-optimization procedure repeatedly incorporates feedback from the Isabelle verifier, using that feedback to guide subsequent proof generation.

On miniF2F-test, fine-tuning only on the PSR-selected data achieves 84.8% Pass@64. Adding dynamic verifier-based prompt optimization raises this to 90.6%, which the authors report as a new state of the art for Isabelle neural theorem proving. Pass@64 measures success across a budget of 64 attempts, so these results describe multi-attempt proving performance. Together, they show the benefits of curated proof data and responsive use of formal verification.
icml-2026-enhancing-neural-theorem-provi.tldr: Selecting diverse, informative Isabelle proofs and incorporating verifier feedback raises reported miniF2F-test performance to 90.6% Pass@64.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models offer the possibility of higher generation throughput, but improving their reasoning requires reinforcement-learning methods suited to their structure. This paper introduces Distribution Matching Policy Optimization, or DMPO, as a theoretically grounded way to fine-tune these models using rewards.

DMPO trains the model to match an optimal reward-tilted distribution: a target distribution that favors outputs according to their rewards. It performs this matching through cross-entropy optimization. The authors identify a practical difficulty when training batches are small and develop several remedies using a new weight baseline subtraction technique. Addressing that implementation issue is part of making the distribution-matching objective usable in practice.

Across multiple reasoning benchmarks, DMPO improves performance without supervised fine-tuning. The largest reported accuracy gains are 39.63 percentage points over earlier non-DMPO reinforcement-learning baselines and 67.97 percentage points over the base model. These are maximum gains across the reported evaluations, rather than a uniform improvement on every task. The results support distribution matching as an effective approach to strengthening diffusion-model reasoning.
icml-2026-enhancing-reasoning-for-diffus.tldr: DMPO improves diffusion language-model reasoning by matching a reward-favored target distribution, with large reported gains without supervised fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Understanding a 3D scene requires identifying both what things are and which observations belong to the same individual object. EPS3D addresses these semantic and instance-level tasks together in an open-vocabulary setting. It uses an end-to-end feed-forward framework that predicts 3D-aware features from multiple images of a scene.

Training uses distillation across diverse 3D scenes to improve consistency and avoid error accumulation associated with additional preprocessing. A mutual enhancement module then connects semantic and instance information in both directions. Instance groupings help align semantic predictions within an object, while semantic guidance refines the features used to distinguish object instances.

The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on two benchmarks, including a 13% semantic mIoU improvement on Replica, alongside an example processing time of one second per scene. These results suggest that explicitly coordinating object identity and category information can improve coherent 3D interpretation efficiently. The framework is presented as supporting applications such as robotic manipulation and 3D scene editing, where both kinds of information are useful.
icml-2026-eps3d-end-to-end-feed-forward-.tldr: EPS3D jointly predicts and reconciles semantic and instance features from multi-view images for efficient open-vocabulary 3D scene segmentation.

paragraphs: Video diffusion systems must decode compact latent representations into visible frames. As their diffusion transformers become faster, this decoding step can account for more of the remaining latency. Flash-VAED targets the VAE decoder while preserving compatibility with the original latent distribution, allowing acceleration at this stage of the generation pipeline.

The framework combines two changes. Independence-aware channel pruning removes redundancy among channels, while stage-wise optimization targets the operators that dominate computation, including costly causal 3D convolutions. A three-phase dynamic distillation procedure transfers the original decoder's capabilities into the faster replacement. The design therefore couples architectural efficiency with training intended to retain reconstruction quality.

Experiments on Wan and LTX-Video decoders report approximately sixfold decoder speedup while retaining up to 96.9% of reconstruction performance. For the complete generation pipeline, the reported acceleration reaches 36%, with negligible quality drops on VBench-2.0. The distinction matters: accelerating one component does not multiply the speed of the whole system by the same factor, but it can still deliver a substantial overall improvement.
icml-2026-flash-vaed-plug-and-play-vae-d.tldr: Flash-VAED accelerates video VAE decoding by about sixfold and improves end-to-end generation speed by up to 36%.

paragraphs: Flat objects can be difficult for robots to grasp directly, and differences in shape and material complicate manipulation. Existing approaches often depend on heuristic preparation steps and narrow evaluation settings. This paper separates the problem into choosing a manipulation strategy and executing that strategy through reusable actions.

The strategy generator takes an object's point cloud and learns representations organized around manipulation strategies rather than object identity. Simulated data transformations and contrastive learning support this separation. Given the selected strategy, the execution module breaks a long manipulation sequence into action primitives and dynamically assembles them into stable trajectories.

The authors also introduce FlatLab, a simulation benchmark containing diverse rigid and deformable flat objects. It combines high-fidelity physics, automated multimodal data collection, and standardized tasks and evaluation procedures. Experiments within this benchmark show better performance than existing baselines and effective generalization to unseen objects and categories. The contribution links a reusable manipulation architecture with a common evaluation environment, making broader object variation central to both learning and assessment.
icml-2026-flatlab-a-unified-methodology-.tldr: FlatLab pairs a simulation benchmark with strategy selection and reusable action primitives for manipulating diverse flat objects.

paragraphs: Model merging combines task-specific models into one model at relatively low cost, but it can also carry backdoor behavior into the combined system. Existing defenses that directly edit parameters can suppress unwanted behavior at the expense of ordinary task performance. This paper proposes Linear Feature Path Minimization, or LFPM, to address that tradeoff.

LFPM introduces an anti-backdoor task vector and guides its optimization through the merged model's feature behavior. Its Cross-Task Linearity perspective uses the approximate linearity of features across tasks. This provides a way to target backdoor suppression while seeking to preserve the representations needed for clean tasks, rather than relying only on direct parameter-space changes.

The optimization mechanism combines gradient accumulation with a loss path-integral to suppress backdoors along the interpolation path. Experiments report consistently strong robustness in both full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning settings. The findings support examining how task combinations affect internal features when designing defenses, with protection along the combination path forming an explicit part of the method.
icml-2026-from-parameters-to-feature-spa.tldr: LFPM uses feature-space guidance to optimize an anti-backdoor task vector for merged models while seeking to preserve clean-task performance.

paragraphs: Electronic health records can become very long when represented as text, increasing language-model computation and sometimes reducing prediction quality. Medical Token-Pair Encoding, or MedTPE, compresses these sequences by extending tokenization. It replaces frequently co-occurring medical token pairs with composite tokens, preserving information rather than discarding less prominent parts of the record.

The method applies these merges in layers and uses dependency-aware replacement to preserve computational complexity. Learning focuses only on the embeddings of newly added tokens, representing 0.5–1.0% of the language model's parameters. These embeddings are fine-tuned through self-supervised learning, allowing the model to use the compressed vocabulary without updating its full parameter set.

Experiments across multiple language models and four clinical prediction tasks report input-length reductions of up to 31% and inference-latency reductions of 34–63%. Predictive performance and output-format compliance are maintained or improved. The authors also report robustness across context lengths and generalization to scientific and financial domains and different languages. The results indicate that changing how recurring information is encoded can reduce processing costs while retaining useful content.
icml-2026-from-token-to-token-pair-effic.tldr: MedTPE losslessly compresses recurring medical token pairs, reducing sequence length and inference latency while maintaining or improving evaluated prediction performance.

paragraphs: Text-to-image models can follow a prompt accurately yet produce a narrow range of images for it. GASS approaches this diversity problem through the geometry of image and text representations. Its aim is to control variation associated with the prompt separately from variation that is independent of the prompt.

The method decomposes diversity in CLIP embedding space along two perpendicular directions. The text-embedding direction represents prompt-related semantic variation, while an identified orthogonal direction represents variation such as backgrounds. GASS increases the spread of projected image embeddings along both directions and uses expanded predictions throughout the generation trajectory to guide sampling.

Experiments test the approach on frozen image-generation backbones spanning U-Net and Transformer architectures, as well as diffusion and flow models. The authors report improved diversity with minimal effects on image fidelity and semantic alignment. These findings suggest that explicitly separating sources of variation can broaden generated outputs while largely retaining their relevance to the prompt. The contribution is a sampling intervention that works across the evaluated model families without retraining those backbones.
icml-2026-gass-geometry-aware-spherical-.tldr: GASS guides image sampling along separate prompt-related and prompt-independent directions to increase diversity with minimal reported quality impact.

paragraphs: A traveler must decide whether to pay ordinary trip costs or buy a card that provides discounts for a fixed period. Trips arrive over time, so decisions must be made without seeing the complete future schedule. The objective includes both travel spending and card purchases, making the timing of each purchase important.

The paper asks how much an offline sample of trips can improve this online decision problem. Such a sample might come from a model trained on historical data. Without this additional information, the best deterministic competitive ratio is 2: a worst-case comparison with the optimal cost achievable with full knowledge of the input.

The authors show that even a sparse sample can improve the ratio to 3/2, with a ratio close to 1 under additional conditions. Numerical simulations support the theoretical bounds and find nearly optimal solutions for several natural input classes. The result demonstrates how limited advance information can sharpen online decisions, while the strongest near-optimal guarantee remains dependent on the stated additional conditions.
icml-2026-learning-augmented-rent-or-buy.tldr: An offline trip sample improves rent-or-buy guarantees from a competitive ratio of 2 to 3/2, and near 1 under additional conditions.

paragraphs: A valid demonstration does not necessarily teach a robot what it still needs to learn. Under a limited demonstration budget, this is especially difficult for novice teachers who cannot inspect the robot's learning mechanisms. CLASP helps connect observed failures to changes a teacher can make in subsequent demonstrations.

The framework builds a compact map of behavioral regions anchored in the teacher's own demonstrations. This gives the teacher a familiar reference for understanding where learning is going wrong. The same map supports difficulty-aware training, which places more emphasis on regions where the policy continues to fail. It therefore informs both human teaching choices and the learner's allocation of training effort.

Across diverse benchmarks, CLASP improves success by up to 20% over offline and interactive baselines using the same demonstration budget. It also reports 14–20% improvements in robustness under distribution shift while preserving behavioral diversity. These findings suggest that making weaknesses understandable and actionable can increase the value of limited demonstrations, without relying solely on collecting more examples.
icml-2026-making-learner-weakness-action.tldr: CLASP maps robot learning failures onto familiar demonstrations so novice teachers and training procedures can target remaining weaknesses.

paragraphs: Bayesian prediction represents uncertainty by combining prior information with observed data, but computing it can be expensive. Networks that learn to map datasets directly to predictive distributions offer a faster alternative. Their weakness, as described here, is that predictions remain closely tied to the priors encountered during training, limiting adaptation when those priors change.

This paper introduces a multi-task framework that makes prior information an explicit part of the input. A prefix of in-context datasets represents that information, and a Transformer trains on sequences containing prior and target tasks. The resulting model learns to adjust predictions across families of priors within an amortized hierarchical Bayesian inference framework.

Evaluations include challenging priors outside the meta-training distribution, covering heavy-tailed behavior and high-dimensional latent structures. The authors report matching oracle Bayesian predictors while running orders of magnitude faster. They also demonstrate the method on a real-world spatiotemporal temperature-prediction benchmark. These results support task-based context as a practical mechanism for adapting fast Bayesian prediction to changing prior information.
icml-2026-multi-task-bayesian-in-context.tldr: A Transformer uses prior-task datasets as context to adapt Bayesian predictions across prior families, matching evaluated oracle predictors much faster.

paragraphs: Spending more computation during generation can improve language-model reasoning, but deciding which partial solutions deserve that computation is crucial. Sequential Monte Carlo repeatedly generates, evaluates, rejects, and resamples reasoning trajectories. A reward model guides these choices, even though practical systems only have approximations to the true rewards.

This paper provides a theoretical condition under which those approximations are sufficient. It identifies the approximate reward model's Bellman error as the key quantity governing the effectiveness of Sequential Monte Carlo. For a reasoning process with T steps, the authors show that a Bellman error bounded on the order of 1/T enables a change in computational complexity from exponential to polynomial in T.

The result establishes a conditional exponential efficiency improvement despite imperfect rewards. Its significance is that exact reward evaluation is not required for this theoretical benefit; a sufficiently controlled approximation can suffice. The error condition becomes more demanding as the reasoning process grows longer. The claim therefore connects the quality of intermediate evaluation to the potential computational benefit of inference-time search.
icml-2026-on-the-power-of-approximate-re.tldr: The paper proves that sufficiently small Bellman error lets approximate reward models give Sequential Monte Carlo an exponential reasoning-efficiency improvement.

paragraphs: Research illustrations must communicate scientific content clearly while remaining visually readable. Producing them is still labor-intensive even as other parts of research become more automated. PaperBanana addresses this step with a framework that coordinates specialized agents powered by vision-language and image-generation models.

The workflow includes retrieving references, planning content and visual style, rendering an image, and refining it through self-critique. Separating these activities gives the system explicit stages for deciding what a figure should communicate and how it should look. Iterative review then provides a mechanism for revising the rendered result rather than stopping after the first image.

The authors introduce PaperBananaBench, containing 292 methodology-diagram test cases curated from NeurIPS 2025 publications across varied research areas and styles. Experiments report consistent improvements over leading baselines in faithfulness, conciseness, readability, and aesthetics. They also demonstrate extension to statistical plots. These findings support coordinated planning and revision as a useful approach to academic illustration, with evaluation covering both communication quality and visual presentation.
icml-2026-paperbanana-automating-academi.tldr: PaperBanana coordinates reference retrieval, planning, rendering, and self-critique to automate academic diagrams and statistical plots.

paragraphs: A partially hidden object can admit several plausible 3D interpretations, so an image alone may not reveal its category or unseen shape. This paper formalizes a task in which text directs completion of the hidden regions while the visible observation must remain strictly preserved. The challenge is to make these two forms of guidance cooperate.

RelaxFlow assigns them different levels of control. Its training-free dual-branch framework combines a Multi-Prior Consensus Module with a Relaxation Mechanism, keeping observation constraints rigid while allowing the prompt to guide broader structure. The authors prove that the relaxation is equivalent to low-pass filtering the generative vector field, suppressing fine instance details to isolate geometry that can accommodate the observation.

The paper introduces ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D as diagnostic benchmarks. Experiments show that RelaxFlow can steer unseen regions toward the prompt's intended meaning without compromising visual fidelity. The central contribution is a principled separation of precise visual constraints from more flexible semantic guidance, addressing the ambiguity inherent in reconstructing objects from incomplete views.
icml-2026-relaxflow-text-driven-amodal-3.tldr: RelaxFlow separates rigid observation constraints from flexible text guidance to complete hidden 3D geometry without compromising visible fidelity.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts language models save computation by activating only a few experts for each token. However, when memory can hold only a small expert cache, changing experts frequently requires costly transfers from external storage. ReMoE addresses this data-movement bottleneck by changing routing behavior through fine-tuning.

The framework biases the router toward experts selected recently. This makes consecutive routing decisions more stable and increases the chance that needed experts are already cached. By encouraging short-horizon reuse, it reduces storage fetches without introducing additional computation at inference time. The intervention aligns model routing with the practical constraints of limited memory.

Experiments on DeepSeek and Qwen models report 26% higher expert reuse while maintaining downstream task performance. System evaluations show 8.4% higher output throughput with vLLM GPU–CPU expert offloading. On Jetson Orin NX using llama.cpp, time per output token falls by 43.6–49.8%, corresponding to 1.77–1.99-fold decoding speedups. These results illustrate that reducing expert movement can translate into substantial speed gains, with the magnitude depending on the evaluated deployment.
icml-2026-remoe-boosting-expert-reuse-th.tldr: ReMoE fine-tunes expert routing to favor recent experts, reducing memory-transfer overhead and accelerating constrained MoE inference.

paragraphs: Continuously structured measurements, such as signals from monitoring or sensing, can contain complex relationships concentrated in particular regions. Conventional functional models can be limited by linearity, while deep models may struggle to identify interpretable regions of influence. This paper introduces sBayFDNN to combine nonlinear prediction with structured region selection.

The model learns adaptive functional embeddings through a deep Bayesian architecture. A structured prior encourages selection of influential regions and quantifies uncertainty about them. This brings prediction and interpretation into the same model: it can represent complex dependencies while indicating which portions of the functional domain contribute to those relationships.

The authors establish approximation-error bounds, posterior consistency, and region-selection consistency, reporting these as the first theoretical guarantees for a Bayesian deep functional model. Simulations and real-world studies also show strong predictive performance and more precise identification of meaningful regions. The contribution combines empirical effectiveness with mathematical support for both learning the underlying relationships and selecting relevant regions, rather than treating interpretability as a separate analysis after prediction.
icml-2026-sparse-bayesian-deep-functiona.tldr: sBayFDNN combines nonlinear functional prediction, uncertainty-aware region selection, and theoretical guarantees in a deep Bayesian model.

paragraphs: Indirect reciprocity means helping someone because they have helped others. Sustaining this behavior among decentralized, self-interested language-model agents requires some way to assess reputations. ALIGN investigates whether strategically shared linguistic gossip can supply that information and support cooperation without a centralized reputation system.

The framework lets agents exchange open-ended gossip with hierarchical tones, form reputations, judge trustworthiness, and coordinate social norms. In the reported evaluations, it consistently improves indirect reciprocity and resists malicious entrants by identifying and excluding defectors. Reputation formation therefore affects who receives cooperation, making exchanged judgments part of the agents' strategic decision process.

The authors also find that stronger reasoning capabilities lead to cooperation that better matches incentives. Chat models often cooperate excessively even when doing so is strategically unfavorable. This distinction matters because a higher amount of cooperation does not by itself demonstrate better decisions for self-interested agents. The findings suggest decentralized gossip combined with reasoning as a promising mechanism for maintaining social welfare in agent populations.
icml-2026-talk-judge-cooperate-gossip-dr.tldr: ALIGN uses decentralized gossip to build agent reputations, improve indirect reciprocity, and identify defectors in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Generating images of the same object from different viewpoints requires those images to agree about what they depict. ViewMask-1-to-3 approaches this task as discrete sequence modeling. Each view is encoded as visual tokens from MAGVIT-v2, allowing generation to operate through token prediction in a shared language-and-vision representation.

The model progressively fills masked tokens through discrete diffusion. Random masking and self-attention encourage agreement across views without specialized architectural components or explicit 3D geometric priors. This makes the relationship between viewpoints something the token model learns through its shared prediction process, rather than something imposed through a dedicated geometric design.

On GSO and 3D-FUTURE, the authors report stronger performance than the baseline and first-place average ranking across standard image metrics. On 3D-FUTURE, they report 10.6% higher IoU than continuous diffusion models. The framework can also be extended to text-to-image generation and multimodal understanding. These results support discrete masked-token generation as a promising common foundation for multiple visual and language-related tasks.
icml-2026-viewmask-1-to-3-multi-view-con.tldr: ViewMask-1-to-3 generates consistent viewpoints through iterative visual-token unmasking without specialized architectures or explicit 3D priors.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation assigns labels throughout an image using text queries. This paper pursues an efficient, training-free approach with the spatially aware dino.txt framework. Although dino.txt captures spatial information well, the authors find that ambiguous text queries can still produce serious mismatches between language and local visual content.

Visual-guided Prompt Evolution, or VIP, improves how those queries express meaning. It combines alias expansion with visually guided distillation to extract useful semantic cues. A saliency-aware aggregation process then combines the cues into the final prediction. The method therefore uses information from the image to improve the language guidance involved in fine-grained object perception.

Evaluations report improvements in average mIoU over leading methods, generalization across challenging domains, and only marginal additional inference time and memory use. These findings indicate that stronger spatial features alone do not resolve every cross-modal mismatch: the wording and interpretation of category queries also matter. VIP contributes a way to refine that semantic interface while retaining the efficiency sought in training-free dense prediction.
icml-2026-vip-visual-guided-prompt-evolu.tldr: VIP refines dino.txt text queries using visual guidance to improve training-free segmentation with little additional inference cost.
